unit: Ch 2: Residential Status and Scope of Total Income
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Basic Concepts of Residential Status
explain: Income-tax liability in India depends on the residential status of the assessee during the tax year.
Residential status must be determined afresh for every tax year.
Residential status and citizenship are two completely distinct legal concepts.
Taxpayers are categorized based on their entity type and degree of stay or control in India.

flow.title: Steps to Determine Tax Liability Basis

topics.example: An Indian citizen who has been residing in the USA for 10 years is a Non-Resident for Indian income-tax purposes.
remember: Residential status is determined for each tax year separately.
Citizenship does not automatically make a person a resident for tax purposes.
mistakes: Assuming an Indian citizen is automatically a resident of India for tax purposes.

quiz.q: How often must an assessee's residential status be determined for income tax purposes?
quiz.why: Residential status must be ascertained separately for each tax year based on stay or control.

quiz.q: Is citizenship the same as residential status under the Income-tax Act?
quiz.why: Residential status depends on physical stay or control, while citizenship depends on nationality.

topics.title: Residential Status of an Individual - Basic Conditions
explain: An individual is a Resident if they satisfy at least one of the two basic conditions.
First Basic Condition: Stay in India for 182 days or more during the relevant tax year.
Second Basic Condition: Stay in India for 60 days or more in the tax year AND 365 days or more in the preceding 4 tax years.
Exception 1: Indian citizen leaving India for employment or as crew of an Indian ship needs 182 days stay (60-day rule does not apply).
Exception 2: Indian citizen/PIO visiting India with Indian income <= Rs. 15 lakhs needs 182 days stay.
Exception 3: Indian citizen/PIO visiting India with Indian income > Rs. 15 lakhs has a modified 120-day requirement instead of 60 days.

flow.title: Individual Residency Decision Flow
steps: Check 182 Days Stay in Tax Year
If No, Check Special Exception Category
If Exception Applies, Test 182 Days Only
If No Exception, Test 60 Days + 365 Days in 4 Years

topics.example: Mr. A leaves India for a new job in London on Sept 20. Since he left for employment, he must stay at least 182 days to be a resident.
remember: Day of arrival and day of departure are both counted as stay in India.
Foreign source income is excluded when calculating the Rs. 15 lakh threshold.
mistakes: Applying the 60-day second basic condition to an Indian citizen leaving India for employment.

quiz.q: An Indian citizen leaves India for the first time on 20th Sept 2026 for employment abroad, staying 172 days in India during T.Y. 2026-27. What is his status?
quiz.why: He left for employment, so only the 182-day rule applies; staying 172 days makes him Non-Resident.

quiz.q: What is the modified stay requirement in the tax year for a visiting PIO with Indian income of Rs. 17 lakhs?
quiz.why: For visiting citizens/PIOs with Indian income > Rs. 15 lakhs, the 60-day rule changes to 120 days.

topics.title: Deemed Resident for Individuals
explain: An individual is deemed to be a resident in India if three cumulative conditions are met.
Condition 1: Must be an Indian citizen.
Condition 2: Total income other than foreign sources exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs during the tax year.
Condition 3: Not liable to tax in any other country by reason of domicile, residence, or similar criteria.
Physical stay in India is NOT required to become a deemed resident under Section 6(7).
A deemed resident under Section 6(7) is ALWAYS classified as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR).

flow.title: Deemed Residency Verification
steps: Check if Individual is Indian Citizen
Check if Indian Income Exceeds Rs. 15 Lakhs
Check if Not Liable to Tax Anywhere Else

topics.example: Mr. K, an Indian citizen living in Dubai (a tax-free country), earns Rs. 18 lakhs from rental property in India. He is a deemed resident in India.
remember: Deemed residents are strictly categorized as RNOR.
Liable to tax means income-tax liability exists under foreign law.
mistakes: Applying deemed residency provisions to a Person of Indian Origin who is not an Indian citizen.

quiz.q: Can a Person of Indian Origin (who is not an Indian citizen) become a deemed resident under Section 6(7)?
quiz.why: Section 6(7) applies exclusively to Indian citizens.

quiz.q: What is the residential sub-category of a deemed resident under Section 6(7)?
quiz.why: Deemed residents u/s 6(7) are always treated as RNOR.

topics.title: Resident Sub-categories: ROR vs RNOR for Individuals
explain: Once an individual is a resident, determine if they are Ordinarily Resident (ROR) or Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR).
An individual is RNOR if they satisfy ANY ONE of the specified conditions u/s 6(13):
1. Non-resident in India in 9 out of 10 tax years preceding the relevant year.
2. Stay in India for 729 days or less during the preceding 7 tax years.
3. Indian citizen/PIO visiting India with Indian income > Rs. 15 lakhs staying between 120 and 181 days.
4. Deemed resident under Section 6(7).
An individual is ROR if they satisfy BOTH: Resident in at least 2 out of 10 preceding years AND stay of 730 days or more in preceding 7 years.

flow.title: Determining ROR vs RNOR Status
steps: Check Resident in >= 2 of 10 Preceding Years
Check Stay >= 730 Days in 7 Preceding Years
If Both Satisfied -> ROR, Else -> RNOR

topics.example: Mrs. Neha stayed in India for 190 days in 2026-27 but was a non-resident in 8 out of 10 preceding years. She is a resident but RNOR.
remember: 730 days stay in preceding 7 years is required for ROR.
Deemed residents u/s 6(7) are automatically RNOR.
mistakes: Assuming a resident individual is ROR without verifying the historical 7-year and 10-year conditions.

quiz.q: A resident individual stayed in India for 800 days in the last 7 years but was non-resident in 9 out of 10 preceding years. What is her status?
quiz.why: Being non-resident in 9 out of 10 preceding years satisfies the RNOR condition.

quiz.q: How many days of stay in India during the preceding 7 years are required to potentially qualify as ROR?
quiz.why: ROR requires a cumulative stay of 730 days or more in the preceding 7 tax years.

topics.title: Period of Stay for Indian Ship Crew Members
explain: For an Indian citizen who is a crew member of a foreign-bound ship, stay in India excludes specific voyage periods.
Excluded Period: From the date entered in Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC) for joining the ship up to the date of signing off.
Eligible Voyage: A voyage by a ship engaged in international traffic originating from or terminating in an Indian port.
Total stay in India is calculated after deducting the CDC continuous excluded days from 365 days.

flow.title: Calculating Stay for Ship Crew
steps: Identify Date of Joining in CDC
Identify Date of Signing Off in CDC
Subtract Excluded Days from Total Tax Year Days

topics.example: Mr. Anand joins a ship on June 6 and signs off on Dec 9 (187 days in CDC). His stay in India is 365 - 187 = 178 days (Non-Resident).
remember: Both entry date of joining and exit date of signing off in CDC are excluded.
Eligible voyage must involve international traffic starting or ending in India.
mistakes: Counting days spent on the ship outside Indian territorial waters without checking official CDC entries.

quiz.q: Which document's dates are used to exclude voyage days for ship crew under Rule 8?
quiz.why: Rule 8 specifically relies on joining and signing-off dates entered in the CDC.

quiz.q: If a crew member's CDC excluded period is 187 days in a 365-day year, what is his calculated stay in India?
quiz.why: Stay in India = 365 - 187 = 178 days.

topics.title: Residential Status of Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)
explain: A HUF is Resident if control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India.
A HUF is Non-Resident if control and management is situated wholly outside India.
Control and management refers to central decision-making (where head and brain resides), not day-to-day operations.
A resident HUF is ROR if Karta satisfies BOTH additional conditions (Resident in >= 2 of 10 preceding years AND stay >= 730 days in 7 preceding years).
If Karta fails either condition, the resident HUF is RNOR.
topics.example: A HUF's policy decisions are taken partly in Delhi and partly in Dubai. The HUF is resident in India.
remember: Even partial control in India makes the HUF resident.
Karta's individual residential status determines whether a resident HUF is ROR or RNOR.
mistakes: Checking Karta's physical stay to determine if the HUF itself is resident or non-resident.

quiz.q: When does a HUF become a Non-Resident in India?
o: When control & management is wholly outside India
When control & management is partly outside India
quiz.why: HUF is non-resident only when control and management is situated wholly outside India.

quiz.q: Who must satisfy additional conditions to make a resident HUF an ROR?
quiz.why: The status of ROR/RNOR for a resident HUF depends on the Karta satisfying the additional conditions.

topics.title: Residential Status of Firms, AOPs, BOIs & Other Entities
explain: A Firm, AOP, BOI, Local Authority, or Artificial Juridical Person is Resident if control and management is situated wholly or partly in India.
They are Non-Resident if control and management is situated wholly outside India.
Residential status of individual partners or members is immaterial while determining the entity's status.
Entities other than Individuals and HUFs can ONLY be Resident or Non-Resident (they cannot be RNOR).

flow.title: Firm/AOP/BOI Residency Test
steps: Wholly or Partly in India -> Resident

topics.example: ABC Partnership Firm has 2 partners in UK and 1 partner in India making key management decisions in Mumbai. The firm is Resident in India.
remember: Firms, AOPs, and BOIs can never be RNOR.
Partners' personal residency does not dictate the firm's residency.
mistakes: Trying to classify a partnership firm as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident.

quiz.q: Can a partnership firm be classified as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)?
o: No, only Individuals and HUFs can be RNOR
quiz.why: Only Individuals and HUFs can be classified into ROR and RNOR sub-categories.

quiz.q: A partnership firm's control is 90% in London and 10% in Delhi. What is its residential status?
quiz.why: Control and management situated even partly in India makes the entity Resident.

topics.title: Residential Status of Companies
explain: A company is Resident in India in any tax year if: (i) it is an Indian company, OR (ii) its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in that year is in India.
A foreign company is Resident ONLY if its POEM is in India. If POEM is outside India, it is Non-Resident.
Place of Effective Management (POEM) means the place where key management and commercial decisions necessary for business conduct are made in substance.
An Indian company is ALWAYS resident in India, regardless of where its POEM or operations are located.

flow.title: Company Residency Determination
steps: If Foreign Company -> Check POEM Location
POEM in India -> Resident; POEM Outside -> Non-Resident

topics.example: XYZ Ltd is incorporated in India but carries on all business operations in London. It is still a Resident company because it is an Indian company.
remember: An Indian company is ALWAYS a resident of India.
Foreign company residency depends entirely on POEM.
mistakes: Evaluating POEM for an Indian company (Indian companies are automatically resident).

quiz.q: An Indian company carries on its entire business from London. What is its residential status in India?
quiz.why: An Indian company is always a resident in India irrespective of where its operations/POEM are located.

quiz.q: What determines the residential status of a foreign company?
quiz.why: A foreign company is resident in India only if its POEM is in India during that tax year.

topics.title: Scope of Total Income
explain: Taxability of income in India depends on residential status and place of accrual/receipt.
Resident & Ordinarily Resident (ROR): Global income is taxable in India (received or accrued anywhere in the world).
Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR): Taxable on Indian income PLUS foreign income derived from a business controlled in or profession set up in India.
Non-Resident (NR): Taxable ONLY on income received/deemed to be received in India OR accruing/arising/deemed to accrue or arise in India.
Income received outside India and later remitted to India is NOT treated as received in India.

flow.title: Scope of Income Matrix
steps: If RNOR -> Tax Indian Income + Foreign Business Controlled from India
If NR -> Tax Indian Income Only

topics.example: Rent from property in London deposited in a London bank is taxable for ROR, but NOT taxable for RNOR or Non-Resident.
remember: First receipt determines taxability; remittance to India is not receipt.
Non-residents are never taxed on purely foreign income.
mistakes: Treating remittance of foreign income to India as receipt of income in India.

quiz.q: Is foreign income from a business controlled outside India taxable in the hands of an RNOR?
quiz.why: RNOR is only taxed on foreign income if derived from a business controlled in or profession set up in India.

quiz.q: Which category of assessee is liable to tax on global income in India?
quiz.why: ROR pays tax on global income accruing or received anywhere in the world.

topics.title: Income Deemed to be Received
explain: Income actual or deemed to be received in India is taxable for ALL taxpayers regardless of residential status.
Deemed received income includes annual accretion to RPF in excess of 9.5% p.a. interest or employer contribution > 12% of salary.
Transferred balance from Unrecognized Provident Fund (URPF) to Recognized Provident Fund (RPF) is deemed received.
Employer contribution to an employee pension scheme u/s 80CCD/124 is deemed received.
Receipt refers strictly to the FIRST occasion money comes under the recipient's control.
topics.example: Interest credited to an employee's RPF account at 11% p.a. is deemed received in India to the extent of the 1.5% excess over 9.5%.
remember: First control over money constitutes receipt; subsequent remittance is not receipt.
Interest on RPF above 9.5% p.a. is deemed received.
mistakes: Confusing first receipt of income with subsequent remittance of funds into India.

quiz.q: Interest credited to RPF is deemed to be received in India beyond what annual rate?
quiz.why: Interest credited in excess of 9.5% p.a. to RPF is deemed to be received in India.

quiz.q: Does remittance of foreign income from a bank in London to a bank in India constitute receipt in India?
o: No, receipt refers only to the first occasion
quiz.why: First receipt occurred in London; remittance to India is not a receipt of income.

topics.title: Income Deemed to Accrue or Arise in India - Asset & Capital Gains
explain: Section 9 creates a legal fiction deeming certain incomes to accrue or arise in India even if actual accrual is outside India.
Income from any asset, property, or source of income situated in India is deemed to accrue in India.
Capital gains arising from transfer of a capital asset situated in India are deemed to accrue in India.
Income from business connection in India is deemed to accrue in India (attributable operations only).
Exceptions: Export purchasing, news collection, diamond display, or film shooting by non-citizens/foreign entities are NOT business connections.

flow.title: Deemed Accrual - Property & Capital Assets
steps: If Located in India -> Deemed to Accrue in India
For Capital Asset -> Taxable Irrespective of Transfer Location
Apply Business Connection Exceptions if applicable

topics.example: Mr. X (US resident) sells shares of an Indian company to another non-resident in Dubai. Capital gains are deemed to accrue in India because the capital asset is situated in India.
remember: Location of capital asset determines taxability of capital gains in India.
Purchasing goods in India for export is NOT a business connection.
mistakes: Assuming capital gains on Indian assets sold outside India between non-residents are exempt in India.

quiz.q: A non-resident transfers shares of an Indian company in Singapore and receives payment in Dubai. Are capital gains taxable in India?
o: No, because transfer was outside India
Yes, because the asset is situated in India
No, because payment was in Dubai
Taxable only if seller is PIO
quiz.why: Capital gains from transfer of capital assets situated in India are deemed to accrue in India.

quiz.q: Is purchasing goods in India by a non-resident for export considered a business connection in India?
quiz.why: Export purchasing operations are explicitly exempted from business connection rules u/s 9.

topics.title: Income Deemed to Accrue or Arise in India - Salaries, Dividend, Interest, Royalty & FTS
explain: Salaries: Deemed to accrue in India if earned for services rendered in India. Salary paid by Govt to an Indian citizen for services abroad is deemed to accrue in India (foreign allowances exempt).
Dividend: Dividends paid by an Indian company outside India are deemed to accrue in India.
Interest, Royalty, FTS payable by Govt are ALWAYS deemed to accrue in India.
Interest, Royalty, FTS payable by Resident are deemed to accrue in India UNLESS used for business/income outside India.
Interest, Royalty, FTS payable by Non-Resident are deemed to accrue in India ONLY IF used for business/income in India.
Territorial Nexus Not Required (Sec 9(11)): Interest, Royalty, FTS utilized in India are taxable whether or not rendered in India.

flow.title: Interest, Royalty & FTS Accrual Test
steps: If Govt -> Always Deemed to Accrue in India
If Resident -> Deemed Accrual (Unless Foreign Business/Income)
If Non-Resident -> Deemed Accrual ONLY IF Indian Business/Income

topics.example: A foreign consultant in Sri Lanka provides technical advice for a project in India to an Indian company. FTS is deemed to accrue in India regardless of where services were rendered.
remember: Salary paid by Indian Govt to citizen serving abroad is taxable, but foreign allowances are exempt.
Non-resident to non-resident interest/royalty is taxable ONLY if used for Indian business/income.
mistakes: Thinking FTS is exempt if the non-resident consultant never physically enters India.

quiz.q: Mr. A (NR) borrows money from Mr. B (NR) to invest in shares of an Indian company. Is interest paid by A to B deemed to accrue in India?
o: Yes, because it is an Indian company
No, because money wasn't used for business in India
quiz.why: Interest paid by NR to NR is deemed to accrue in India ONLY if used for business/profession in India.

quiz.q: Foreign allowances paid by the Indian Government to an Indian citizen for services rendered abroad are:
o: Deemed to accrue in foreign country
quiz.why: Salary is taxable in India, but foreign allowances/perquisites paid by Govt are exempt.
